name: Concept Explorer
description: The classic first lesson on a topic: hook, objectives, a clear definition, the core idea explained, a real-world link, a check, and a recap.
audience: Introducing a new concept to any class.

signals.why: your words sound like an introduction
the topic is a concept to understand

slides.guidance: Lesson title for {topic} and a short subtitle that names the class level.
Three things students will be able to do after this lesson on {topic}, in student-friendly words.
A surprising fact or a question that makes a {grade} student curious about {topic}.

variants.guidance: A classroom meme about {topic}. Pick one format from MEME FORMATS that matches the idea, write captions a {grade} student finds funny and that make the correct idea easier to remember. Kind to students, never about a person.

slides.guidance: Define the central term of {topic} in one plain sentence, with one everyday example.
Explain how {topic} works in a few clear points, in the order a student needs them.
Connect {topic} to something a {grade} student sees in daily life.
One question that checks the core idea, not trivia. One clearly correct option, three plausible wrong ones.
Three to five takeaways that match the objectives.
